audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6 seconds — it is almost always up, so 'trade when it is down' means trading inside a short gap, not waiting on a timer. Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s and Feast is 80/70/60s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Feast is a percent-HP true-damage execute that 'bypasses your HP-stacking win condition' and 'reads your HP total', appearing in whys[4], whys[6], spikes[1], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.foe[1]. It also says Soul Furnace lets you out-heal his return damage.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Feast devours a unit for a high amount of TRUE damage, and Cho'Gath grows only if the target dies. It is flat, not percent-health — which inverts the advice: armour and magic resist are worthless against it, but a larger health pool is still a real answer. The derived percentHealth flag contradicts the description, so per the brief I followed the description. Soul Furnace is a shield with a 3-second detonation; it heals nothing.
audit.corrected: Every Feast line restated as flat true damage on 80s that resistances cannot reduce, with the growth coming from devouring minions; the 'out-heal through W' line replaced with the shield's real 3-second detonation.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's Rupture (Q) is the only ability you genuinely fear in this lane — the knockup interrupts your charged Q mid-channel and his W-silence immediately after locks you out of any retaliate. At level 1, farm at Q-tip range and watch his feet; Rupture has a visible telegraph delay and you can step out of the circle if you are not channeling. At level 2 your W-shield comes online and changes the math entirely: let him walk forward for a last-hit, pop W, take the trade, and detonate shield for the damage trade. Level 3 is your window — charged Q from a brush or fog angle, land the stun when Rupture is down, E-shred his armor, and brawl; he cannot disengage and you out-heal the return damage through W.
edits.after: Cho'Gath's Rupture (Q) is the only ability you genuinely fear in this lane — the knockup interrupts your charged Q mid-channel and Feral Scream immediately after silences you out of any answer. At level 1, farm at Q-tip range and watch his feet; Rupture has a visible telegraph delay and you can step out of the circle if you are not channeling. At level 2 Soul Furnace comes online and changes the math: let him walk forward for a last-hit, pop W, take the trade, and detonate it after the 3 seconds. Level 3 is your window — charged Q from brush or fog, land the stun in the gap after a spent Rupture, shred his armour with Roar of the Slayer, and brawl; Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1, so his lockout is not always ready.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 the lane flattens — you both have your full basic kits, Rupture is the matchup-defining cooldown, and neither of you has a decisive item spike yet. Respect the Rupture circle religiously; every trade you attempt must begin with confirming it is on cooldown. At level 6 Cho gains Feast, and this changes the threat profile significantly: his R deals true-damage percentage-HP execute that no amount of W-shield or max-HP stacking fully answers. Do not let him R small-minion-stack his way to a 1000-HP Feast bonus for free — you can contest the R channel with your own Q stun if you are close enough, and denying those stacks early caps his late-game ceiling. Your R (Unstoppable Onslaught) is an engage tool here, not a kill button — use it to close gap after confirming Rupture down, then land the full Q-E-W combo before he can silence.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 the lane flattens — you both have your full basic kits, Rupture is the matchup-defining cast, and neither of you has a decisive item spike yet. Respect the circle religiously, but know it is a flat 6 seconds: you are trading inside the gap after a spent cast, not waiting on a long timer. At level 6 Cho gains Feast and the threat profile changes: it is flat true damage on 80 seconds, so neither armour nor magic resist reduces a point of it, while your raw health pool still does. Do not let him devour big minions for free — every one he eats grows his own health bar and raises his ceiling for the rest of the game. Your R is an engage tool here, not a kill button — close the gap once Rupture is spent, then land the full Q-E-W combo before Feral Scream silences you out of it.

edits.before: Two items in, both of you are enormous HP tanks, but Cho'Gath's Feast stacks mean his R execute scales with your HP total — the very thing that makes you unkillable in other matchups is the number his true-damage R is reading when it decides to one-shot you. Play for front-line engage value and your zombie passive threat rather than solo dueling: walk at his team, absorb CC with W-shield, and let your passive zombie deal damage after death. In splits, you can out-push Cho'Gath easily with R + shove, but avoid over-extending when his R is available — a chunked Sion is an easy Feast stack that doubles as a kill. Win condition at this stage is team-fighting and siege, not 1v1 brawling.
edits.after: Two items in, both of you are enormous HP tanks. Feast hits for a flat chunk of true damage, so armour and magic resist buy you nothing against it — but the health you stack does, which is why the bulk plan still holds up here. Play for front-line engage value and your zombie passive rather than solo dueling: walk at his team, absorb CC with Soul Furnace, and let the passive deal damage after death. In splits you out-push him with R and a shove, but avoid over-extending while Feast is up — a chunked Sion is the one target it actually finishes. Win condition at this stage is team-fighting and siege, not 1v1 brawling.

notes: The important correction is an inversion, not a name: the entry says Feast is a percent-health true-damage execute that punishes HP stacking, so a reader concludes Sion's whole scaling plan is invalid here. Riot's text says flat true damage, with growth coming from devouring a unit. That flips the itemisation logic — resistances are the useless answer, health is not. The percentHealth flag on Feast contradicts the description and I followed the description per the brief. Also: Rupture is a 6-second cooldown, so 'only trade when it is down' had to become 'trade in the gap after it is spent'.
